findings.claim_reviewed: Generosity, learning, pride and Janaka’s attributed cosmic self-claim versus Nārada’s devotion argument.
findings.assessment: 65.10 is Nārada’s question about growing wealth;65.12 is his praise of Gaṇeśa’s devotional generosity;65.13–14 is Janaka’s own claim. Patch preserves the speaker distinctions and does not certify the king as cosmic creator.

findings.claim_reviewed: Nārada departure and deity’s repulsive old-Brahmin test manifestation.
findings.assessment: Narrator65.19 explicitly identifies Gajānana testing royal devotion; Janaka separately wonders whether the guest is God65.26–27. Blood, flies, missing teeth, stumbling/fainting and gate admission are directly supported.

findings.claim_reviewed: The guest first asks food until satisfied and conditionally promises hundred-sacrifice merit; immense servings fail.
findings.assessment: 65.29–30 is the guest’s food/satisfaction request to Janaka, not a personal liberation request by the poor couple. One-mouthful portions and prepared food sufficient for ten thousand65.32–34 are supported. Conditional merit is not recorded as earned.

findings.claim_reviewed: Unquenched appetite exhausts city/village grain; the visitor enters Virocanā and Triśiras’s poor home.
findings.assessment: 65.36–37 presents conjectures by onlookers, not proof of a Rākṣasa identity.65.38–43 explicitly keeps the guest unsatisfied and Janaka downcast.65.44 prints virocanātriśirasor ... dvijayor;66.12 names Virocanā as giver and66.16/22 names Triśiras as embraced devotee. No identification with unrelated epic/asura actors is made.

findings.claim_reviewed: Virocanā and Triśiras are a devoted married pair rather than two unrelated beggars.
findings.assessment: 66.7 speaker label dam-patī and66.19 dam-patī link the previously named pair. Their bare-earth/sky-cover austerity, unasked food, water rites and exclusive image worship are supported. The tiny devotional gift versus ostentation teaching66.9 is preserved.

findings.claim_reviewed: The marital assertion currently cites only66.1–9, where the named pair is contextual.
findings.assessment: The relationship is supported in context, but the stored evidence span should include the actual named-pair attestation65.44 to make the actor allocation independently traceable. This is a locator-strengthening correction, not a rejected spouse relationship.
findings.proposed_action: Add gup5-e-033 alongside gup5-e-034; optionally gup5-e-036 supplies the second explicit couple address.

findings.claim_reviewed: Triśiras is typed SAGE although the reviewed body calls him a Brahmin and devotee.
findings.assessment: 65.44 supplies dvija, and66.22 bhaktaṃ triśirasaṃ. These bodies contain no sage epithet establishing this entity type. This review cannot prove that no other passage calls him a sage; it only checks the evidence assigned to this source-local record.
findings.proposed_action: Use DEVOTEE (or PERSON) for this local entity, unless an independently read passage explicitly establishes SAGE; preserve ID and name.

findings.claim_reviewed: One leftover morning-worship dūrvā and imagined food satisfy the guest.
findings.assessment: 66.11 asks the single sprout;66.12 explicitly makes Virocanā the giver.66.13–14 lists rice, pāyasa, cooked foods, accompaniments and lickable/suckable foods imagined upon it. The guest eats it; stomach-fire ceases and complete satisfaction follows. The patch correctly keeps imagined dishes distinct from physical provisions. Digital66.15 is printed5 between14 and16; body continuity is clear, with no omitted unit inferred.

findings.claim_reviewed: Four-armed reveal holding lotus, axe, rosary and tusk.
findings.assessment: Four arms, trunk, lotus eyes and four listed hand objects are explicit. No extra mount, parentage or weapon gift is inferred.

findings.claim_reviewed: The couple’s final request is devotion in whatever birth OR liberation; deity explicitly assents and vanishes.
findings.assessment: 66.20 requests firm devotion wherever born;66.21 supplies muktiḥ vā and no other wish;66.22 has tathā assent, another embrace of Triśiras and disappearance. Patch preserves the alternatives and does not select one, add wealth, or invent a later death/vehicle. The bounded feeding-test ending is present; COMPLETE for this declared scene is supported, subject to small role/evidence corrections.

findings.claim_reviewed: Kauṇḍinya explains his offering and the history’s hearing/telling benefits.
findings.assessment: Devotional hearing/telling, sons/wealth/enjoyment, devotion and specifically desireless liberation are source-attributed conditions, not a narrated new grant to Virocanā/Triśiras.

findings.claim_reviewed: Aśrayā’s renewed doubt leads to a distinct exact-equal-weight gold request to Indra.
findings.assessment: The Gaṇas resume the enclosing narration, Kauṇḍinya knows Aśrayā’s doubt and commands one sprout and gold neither less nor more; she follows her husband’s word. This is separate from the poor couple’s final wish.

findings.claim_reviewed: 67.26 says three worlds failed to equal one sprout;67.40 says they became equal by the leaf on a scale.
findings.assessment: Both readings are directly present:67.26 trilokyam api nālabhat versus67.40 ... abhavat samam. No lexical or temporal reconciliation can be established from this one witness. Keeping the weighing story PARTIAL and conflict OPEN is appropriate.
findings.proposed_action: Retain both descriptors and require independent edition/Sanskrit collation; no equality result should overwrite the trial.

findings.claim_reviewed: The actual later abode transfer concerns Kauṇḍinya/Aśrayā, not Virocanā/Triśiras.
findings.assessment: 67.32–37 names Aśrayā and husband Kauṇḍinya; their continuous morning/evening worship precedes67.38–39 svadhāma pratyapādayat. Patch correctly assigns the actual joint transport to this enclosing couple, while66 only assents to the other couple’s requested alternatives.

findings.claim_checked: Pulaha attains yoga-peace before the deity visit.
findings.independent_read_finding: 17.56–59 recalls the earlier family-deity teaching, fitness for peace, new instruction, Brahmā’s disappearance and Pulaha’s practice.18.1 explicitly says he gradually attained yoga-peace;2 describes constant meditation and the subsequent visit after an unspecified interval. Peace is not wrongly made a result first obtained from the later boon.

findings.claim_checked: Gaṇeśa causes the heart-resident form to disappear, leading to external recognition.
findings.independent_read_finding: The absorbed sage does not notice the arrival.3 names heart-resident Dhuṇḍhi as made to disappear by Gaṇeśa;4 says the sage cannot see the inner Gaṇeśa and sees Gaṇapa outside.5–6 give rising, bowing, proper worship and joyful hymn. Withdrawal of the internal form and exterior recognition are supported; no killing or destroyed deity is narrated.

findings.claim_checked: Exact iconography and theological descriptions remain attributed to Pulaha’s hymn.
findings.independent_read_finding: The hymn explicitly names Vighnarāja, Vakratuṇḍa, Heramba, Svānanda residence, Lambodara, elephant face/form/ears, mouse-banner and mouse-mounted form, noose and goad, four arms and the four aims. It also praises formless Brahman, yoga, peace, cosmic support, many forms and cosmic functions, and says Vedas, yogins and Śiva/Viṣṇu-headed gods cannot fully praise him. The graph uses hymned_as predicates and source-attribution rather than turning this into a universal physical description. Fine epithet normalization remains outside this targeted review.

20 expressly requests firm devotion without deviation;21 describes love-overwhelmed dancing.22 grants very firm devotion without deviation and says it gives joy. No immortality, fixed term, or additional personal request is present. The populated requested/granted/circumstances fields are supported.

findings.claim_checked: Appearance on Pulaha’s remembrance is separate from hymn reading/hearing efficacy.
findings.independent_read_finding: 23 promises that whenever Pulaha remembers the deity he will see him present near himself.24 gives devotion, enjoyment/liberation and peace-yoga to the hymn.25 identifies the mortal who reads or hears it as gaining all happiness and becoming like Pulaha. The distinct triggers and results in the two records are supported. This does not narrate a later actual repeated appearance or make reading the hymn a condition of Pulaha’s personal sight promise.

findings.claim_checked: The encounter ends with deity disappearance and Pulaha remaining in worship.
findings.independent_read_finding: The narrator expressly says Gaṇādhiśa disappears there after speaking; Pulaha remains there and worships Gaṇādhipa. The1–26 bounded encounter has a real stated ending. No later death or transport for Pulaha is inserted.

findings.claim_checked: Deer-bodied Bharata receives and retains the teaching and meditates on Gaṇeśa.
findings.independent_read_finding: 27 says Bharata in deer form dwells there and hears full knowledge.28 identifies the content as what Brahmā told Pulaha, held continually in Bharata’s heart.29 gives joyful continual Gaṇeśa meditation and residence. This does not independently resolve the earlier17.42–43 grammar or assert that Brahmā directly addressed Bharata.

findings.claim_checked: Attributed reflection and actual deer-body abandonment.
findings.independent_read_finding: 30 introduces Bharata’s own utterance.31 says renunciation and Hari remembrance still led to deer-form through deer attachment.32–33 attribute obstacle victory by Śiva/Viṣṇu and all beings to Vighnarāja grace.34 praises earlier Vaiṣṇava devotion, saṃskāra and excellent knowledge;35–36 praise meeting Pulaha and ongoing Gaṇapatya company and unobstructed worship.37 narrates that in time, with Gaṇeśa devotion and meditation, Bharata abandons the body. No new birth or individual liberation grant is narrated within this chapter. The scoped deer-life ending is supported; earlier17.6–24 was not independently reread in this task.

findings.claim_checked: Recipient-class fidelity in the two otherwise supported benefit records.
findings.independent_read_finding: The shared recipient node is labelled “Readers/hearers or qualified practitioners in Mudgala cosmography benefits” and has only river-benefit evidence.24–25 address mortal readers/hearers of Pulaha’s hymn;32–33 describe Śiva, Viṣṇu and all beings in Bharata’s attributed reflection. The benefit wording and triggers are supported, but these recipient scopes are not the cosmography audience as currently labelled.
findings.requested_correction: Use a source-supported human Pulaha-hymn reader/hearer class for the hymn record, with18.24–25 evidence. For the reflection use a source-supported Śiva/Viṣṇu-and-all-beings collective or appropriate broader existing entity, with18.32–33 evidence. Preserve its attributed-reflection notes and do not convert it into a new personal boon. A genuinely broad existing beneficiary node may be reused only if its identity/label and evidence explicitly encompass these distinct audiences.

findings.claim_checked: Independent print-edition certification, full dense teaching resolution, and later biography.
findings.independent_read_finding: This review establishes direct reading of the complete digital Sanskrit body1–37 and bounded17.56–59 context only. It does not collate a printed edition, resolve17.42–43, read the full earlier deer-origin arc, or establish a later human birth/liberation. before.paraphrase: The child asks the gods not to drive him away by force when they see the demon, but to watch his and the demon’s remarkable encounter. They joyfully yet uncertainly discuss his capacity and bow. Analāsura approaches as dissolution-fire, burning ten directions and devouring humans. The people cry out and sages flee, warning the child to escape before the fire kills him, comparing it with a great predator. Gaṇeśa stands firm like Himavat; they retreat far away, leaving him there.
before.verification_notes: Direct Sanskrit body reading; not independent edition verification. Uncertain Sanskrit clauses identified separately.
